newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya to spend $5.5 bln on energy projects by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Libya to spend $5.5 bln on energy projects by 2001.

text.p: Libya plans to spend more than $5.5 billion on five major energy projects over the next four to five years, a Libyan senior energy official said on Tuesday.

Fouad Hajjaji, manager of maintenance and projects department at the Libyan state-oil company National Oil Corp (NOC) told an energy forum that the projects were only "some of the major projects" currently handled by NOC's subsidiaries.

He listed the projects as follows: Western Libya gas project, NC-115 field development, Faregh field development, Attahady field development, and a coastal gas pipeline extension which will supply Libya's two main cities, Tripoli and Benghazi.
"The combined cost of above projects exceeds $5.5 billion," Hajjaji said.

An official of Italy's Agip SpA earlier this week said in Tunis that the company has reached a framework agreement worth $2.1 billion with NOC for the joint development of some offshore and onshore natural gas and condensate field in Western Libya and the construction of a pipeline to Sicily.
Hajjaji did not give any details of the other projects listed.
Hajjaji said that NOC controls nine affiliated operating companies in Libya, some of which are fully owned and the others set up a joint venture partnership with multinational oil companies.
He said that more than 50 oilfields and five gas fields are currently in production in Libya.

"In recent years new fields in Murzuk and Ghadames Basins in the south west of the country and offshore Libya are also being developed and are expected to be on stream in the near future," Hajjaji said.
Libya presently has also 5,500 km of major oil pipelines and 2,000 km of major gas pipelines, he added.
Hajjaji was talking at a three-day exhibition of oil and gas activities and services attended by more than 140 firms in this southern city of Sfax.
